CVE-2026-110782.title: SAML2: Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-49283: unsigned embedded Response bypasses HTTP-Artifact signature verification (no embedded-Issuer binding)
CVE-2026-110782.description: The SimpleSAMLphp SAML2 library is a PHP library for SAML2 related functionality. From 6.2.2 until 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2, HTTPArtifact::receive() in src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php verifies a signed outer ArtifactResponse but returns an unsigned embedded SAML Response before calling verifyMessageSignature(). The signed path verifies with the artifact issuer's metadata keys without requiring the embedded Response issuer to match that artifact issuer. In a multi-IdP federation, an attacker controlling one trusted IdP can therefore return a validly signed outer ArtifactResponse containing an unsigned Response that claims a different IdP, bypassing the binding's embedded-message authentication. End-to-end impersonation requires a service provider using HTTP-Artifact and a downstream consumer that relies on the binding to authenticate the embedded Response rather than independently requiring a signature. This issue is fixed in versions 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2.

CVE-2026-98912.title: ALSA: seq: oss: Reject reads that cannot fit the next event
CVE-2026-98912.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: seq: oss: Reject reads that cannot fit the next event

snd_seq_oss_read() checks whether the next queued OSS sequencer event
fits in the remaining userspace buffer before removing it from the read
queue.

The check is inverted. It currently stops when the event is smaller than
the remaining buffer, so a normal 4-byte event is not copied for an
8-byte read buffer. Conversely, an 8-byte event can be copied for a
smaller read count.

Break only when the remaining userspace buffer is smaller than the next
event, and report -EINVAL if no complete event has been copied. This
prevents an undersized read from looking like end-of-file while leaving
the event queued for a later read with a large enough buffer.

CVE-2026-99348.title: afs: Fix afs to abort the rxrpc call on send error
CVE-2026-99348.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

afs: Fix afs to abort the rxrpc call on send error

Fix afs_send_empty_reply() and afs_send_simple_reply() to always try to
abort the rxrpc call rather than just aborting on -ENOMEM and otherwise
abandoning it. If the call is already complete due to network failure or a
received abort, this will do nothing.

Also make afs_make_call() always abort on send error; again, it does
nothing if the rxrpc call is already dead.

CVE-2026-99414.title: ovl: skip copy up of empty security.capability
CVE-2026-99414.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: skip copy up of empty security.capability

ovl_copy_xattr() gives up if it can't read an attribute that
listxattr() has named. An empty security.capability, which anybody has
been able to store on any file for a long time, is such a case: it is
listed, and getxattr() has nothing to return for it. A file in a lower
layer that carries one can't be copied up: it can't be written to,
renamed or have its mode changed.

There is nothing to copy if there are no data. Go on with the next
one.

CVE-2026-99667.title: mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp()
CVE-2026-99667.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp()

try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the PTE lock after it has cleared the
page table, and takes the PMD lock and the PTE lock to remove it.

In between, MADV_DONTNEED with CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM can reclaim the
page table. The pmd_same() check is supposed to handle this, but it is
only done with CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS.

Fix it by performing the check unconditionally.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.
